NORTH﷓WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE LOCAL COUNCILS (REMOVAL OF CHAIRMAN,
VICE﷓CHAIRMAN OR MEMBER) RULES, 1994
NORTH‑WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE LOCAL COUNCILS (REMOVAL
OF CHAIRMAN, VICE‑CHAIRMAN OR MEMBER) RULES, 1994
[Gazette of N.‑W.F.P., Extraordinary, 17th August,
1994]
No. AO(LG) 1(60)/90, dated 7‑2‑1994.‑‑In
exercise of the powers conferred by section 172, of the North‑West
Frontier Province Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (N: W.F.P. Ord. IV of 1979),
read with section 34, therefore, the Government of the North‑West
Frontier Province is pleased to make the following rules namely:‑‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑‑(l) These
rules may be called the North‑West Frontier Province Local Councils
(Removal of Chairman, Vice- Chairman or Member) Rules, 1994.
(2) They shall come into force at once.
2. Definition.‑‑In these rules, unless
otherwise provided, the following expression shall have the meanings hereby
respectively assigned to them, that is to say.
(a) `respondent' means Chairman, Vice‑Chairman or a
member against whom proceedings are. initiated under section 34 of the
Ordinance;
(b) Ordinance means the North‑West Frontier Province
Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (Ord. IV of 1979); and
(c) "Complaint, means a complaint under subsection
(1) of section 34 of the Ordinance.
3. Institution of Proceedings.‑‑Any
proceedings under subsection (1) of section 34 of the North‑West Frontier
Province Local Government Ordinance, 1979 for removal of a respondent may be
initiated, by the Government either suo motu or on a complaint.
4. Procedure for complaint.‑‑(l) A complaint
against a respondent shall be addressed to the Government or an Officer
authorised by it in this behalf, who shall as soon as possible place the
complaint before the Government.
(2) No complaint under sub‑rule (1) shall be
entertained unless it is accompanied by an affidavit of the complainant about
the facts stated or allegations levelled in the complaint and such documents or
its attested copies in support thereof, as are in possession of the
complainant.
(3) Upon receipt of a complaint, the Government may take
all or ante of the following actions:‑‑
(a) dismiss the complaint for reasons to be recorded; or
(b) call for the comments of the respondent within a time
to be specified; or
(c) call for a report from officer or any person as deemed
fit; or
(d) call for any other information as may be necessary for
proper disposal of the complaint.
(4) On the receipt of comments or reports under sub‑rule
(3) the Government may,‑‑‑
(a) dismiss the complaint for reasons to be recorded; or
(b) Order the removal of the respondent subject to the
provision rule 5; or
(c) direct that a formal inquiry into the allegations be
conducted by such Officer as it may appoint and on receipt of the inquiry
report pass such orders it deems fit.
(5) The Government may initiate proceedings against the
complainant under section 181 or 182 of Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 if in its
opinion the complaint, or the affidavit in support thereof is false or
frivolous.
5. Conduct of Inquiry.‑‑(1) Any inquiry, if
conducted under sub‑rule (4) of rule 3, shall be conducted in the
presence of the respondent or his authorised agent and shall be completed
within such period as may be specified by the Government..
Provided that any inquiry shall not stand vitiated if it
is not completed within the specified period.
(2) Where the respondent fails to join the proceedings in
spite of notice or wilfully tries to hamper or impede the progress of an
inquiry, the proceedings may be taken ex parte against him or in such other
manner as may be considered appropriate.
(3) In conducting the Inquiry, the Inquiry Officer shall
be deemed to be a tribunal, and shall exercise all the powers vested in a
tribunal under the North‑West Frontier Province Tribunals of Inquiries
Ordinance, 1961 and the proceedings shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings
within the meaning of sections 193 and 228 of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.
